**Hypothesis (final answer):** The domain in which both original and replication studies predominantly used student subjects is **Social** (social psychology, i.e., the "Social" discipline of the original papers). Within the Social discipline, roughly 82–85% of original studies and 78–82% of replication studies used student samples — the closest alignment with the quoted figures (original 82.4%, replication 80.9%). By contrast, Cognitive studies used students less often in the originals (~71–76%), and Economics — although almost entirely student-based (~94–100%) — comprises only 18 small pairs and is far from the quoted percentages. Hence the domain matching the question is Social.

**Explicit caveat (as requested by the researcher):** The exact quoted figures (82.4% / 80.9%) could not be reproduced exactly from the supplied CSV under any simple subset, filter, or weighting we tried; they are treated as approximate values from the source publication. The domain selection rests on the closest alignment between the observed shares and those quoted values, which is unambiguous: Social has the smallest combined distance to (82.4%, 80.9%) at both the pair level (3.8 pp) and the row level (2.6 pp), versus Cognitive (7.6 / 13.9 pp) and Economics (31.1 / 31.1 pp).

Cognitive originals used students less often (~71-76%), and Economics, though nearly all student-based (~94-100%), has only 18 pairs and does not match the quoted percentages. Note: the exact quoted figures could not be reproduced exactly from the CSV under any simple cut and are treated as approximate source-publication values; domain selection is based on closest alignment.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded the study-level CSV (927 rows, 141 unique O/R pair ids; projects ml1/ml3/rpp/ee) and quantified missingness (subjects.o 1, subjects.r 1, discipline 0, project 0). 2) Deduplicated to one row per pair id, preferring the aggregated==True row (26 ids) else the first row; verified subjects.o is constant within every id and discipline is constant within every id. 3) Computed the share of subjects=='students' per discipline (Social, Cognitive, Economics) for subjects.o and subjects.r at the pair level (main) and at the row/lab level (sensitivity), counting 'anyone', 'community', 'online' and NaN as non-students. 4) Sensitivity checks: excluded the 10 pair ids entirely flagged drop==True; examined the 16 ml1 ids whose subjects.r varies across labs (aggregated rows all record 'students'); handled the single missing-subjects row rpp.154 by excluding it from denominators. 5) Computed a joint measure (both original and replication used students) and the distance of each discipline's shares to the quoted 82.4%/80.9%; Social is closest at both levels, so the answer is Social. 6) The second CSV (143 rows) has no subjects/discipline columns and was used only to verify project naming. Supporting outputs: outputs/analysis_output.txt (console log), outputs/students_by_discipline_pair_level.csv, outputs/students_by_discipline_row_level.csv.
